Principle.1: Bonuses live at tier 1, if anywhere. A tier-1 effect reads "gain X when you do Y" and is gated.
Principle.2: Higher tiers widen the circumstances, not the size. Tier 2: "when Y or Z". Tier 3: "…even when [unusual condition]". The bonus never grows.
Principle.3: Tier 3 is more focused, not more powerful. A tier-3 effect that works in every circumstance is a design failure; it needs a ceiling that creates real blind spots.
Principle.4: A tier-1 circumstance sets the identity of everything above it.
Principle.5: Talents that push a secondary up a tier situationally are a legitimate build axis.
Principle.6: Groups that thrive under conditions another group creates are natural cross-prerequisites.
